defect: stored XSS / content-type spoofing on document serving
original_reproduction: Run-41 section 2 re-reproduced on current v25 (not taken from the Run-40 artifact): an authenticated PM uploads bytes via POST /exec action=projectupload with an attacker-chosen mimeType. The client-supplied MIME is stored verbatim (no upload validation) and echoed by the serve route as Content-Type with Content-Disposition: inline and no nosniff. Real Chromium proof (code_audit/run41_s1_prefix_browser_proof.json): 4 of 4 attacker payloads (quarterly.pdf+text/html, payload.html+text/html, chart.svg+image/svg+xml, chart.png+text/html) reached the serving boundary with HTTP 200 and EXECUTED script inside the application origin when loaded in a same-origin iframe, exactly as assets/js/files.js previews documents. Evidence: code_audit/run41_s1_prefix_reproduction.json.
owner_disposition: FIX BEFORE PARTICIPANT USE (do not accept for the study period)
intended_minimal_remediation: Server-controlled response content type at the serving boundary: Content-Type drawn from an inline-safe allowlist that browsers render without script (application/pdf, png, jpeg, gif, webp, text/plain); anything else - including text/html, image/svg+xml, xhtml and xml - served as application/octet-stream with Content-Disposition: attachment; X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on every response; Content-Disposition filename sanitised so a quote, backslash or control character cannot break the quoted-string or split the response. Stored bytes, authorization and extraction untouched.
qualification_affected: freeze qualification (server/app is a frozen-immutability surface), study-execution readiness, main-study launch readiness, functional/security acceptance

defect: final-lock database integrity gap on primary outcome data
original_reproduction: Run-41 section 5 reproduced on current v25 schema in an isolated SQLite: a decision was driven to final lock entirely through the real application routes (researchevidenceget -> researchprejudgment (submit+lock in one statement) -> researchreveal -> researchdecision, which sets final_submitted_at = the final lock). With final_submitted_at set, 13 of 13 direct raw-SQL UPDATE statements against the decisions row SUCCEEDED, silently altering every substantive final-response field and even clearing final_submitted_at itself. No trigger, no updated_at, no audit row. Evidence: code_audit/run41_s2_prefix_reproduction.json.
affected_route_or_state: decisions table after final_submitted_at is set (persisted final participant judgment)
owner_disposition: FIX BEFORE PARTICIPANT USE (do not accept for the study period)
intended_minimal_remediation: A final-lock database trigger mirroring the existing trg_decisions_pre_lock_guard (migration 0003), added through the governed alembic mechanism as migration 0026 with both a Postgres plpgsql function/trigger and a SQLite BEFORE UPDATE trigger. Refuses any UPDATE that would change a substantive final-response field once final_submitted_at is set, and refuses clearing or moving final_submitted_at itself (without which the guard is trivially bypassed in two statements). Protected set derived mechanically from the live model, not from prose - see code_audit/run41_final_judgment_field_derivation.csv. Pre-lock writes are unaffected.
qualification_affected: freeze qualification, study-execution readiness, main-study launch readiness, functional/security acceptance, lock/state-machine gates
